statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk is 22% (watch) because the NQ session high advanced to 30,961.50 and price is holding roughly 7 points below it, while Stress of 56% (elevated) reflects a 10-year yield at 5.167% in its sixth consecutive weekly climb against roughly 77% odds of an October Fed increase.
recommendation: Tail has re-entered the WATCH band and remains below the block threshold. The concentrated whipsaw window is 12:15-15:15 UTC, covering August durable goods orders at 12:30 UTC, the US cash open at 13:30 UTC, the final September Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations release at 14:00 UTC and the delayed second-leg hour that can follow. Cleveland Fed President Hammack is scheduled at 18:00 UTC. US cash markets close at 20:00 UTC and CME equity index futures close for the week at 21:00 UTC, reopening at 22:00 UTC on Sunday; forecast hours inside that halt carry reduced Confidence because no live price path exists to observe.
headline: The NQ session high extends to 30,961.50 and price holds just below it, returning Tail to the WATCH band while a 15.3 VIX, flat yields and split megacaps leave the amplifier stack unaligned
body:
NQ December futures trade at 30,954.75, up 188.00 points or 0.61%, with the session recorded between 30,679.00 and 30,961.50 from a 30,726.50 open. The decisive change from the previous hour is structural rather than directional: the session high has advanced from 30,906 to 30,961.50, and price is holding roughly 7 points below the new extreme instead of retracing 25-32 points from a static one.

That combination is extension after the prior high was cleared, together with price holding near the extreme. Those are two of the named amplifiers, so Tail returns to the WATCH band it occupied at 06:00 and 07:00 UTC. It does not reach the block threshold, because the structure required for that is repeated extension after failed retracements sustained over several hours, and the observed band remains only about 0.92% wide on an orderly overnight grind.

Cross-asset evidence does not confirm a one-way path. VIX is 15.31, down 2.30%, inside an unusually tight 15.29-15.64 range. The 10-year yield is 5.167%, up 0.4 basis points, in a 5.153-5.189% range and short of its 5.227% 52-week high, while the 2-year is near 4.899%; the long end is firm rather than extending, although this is the sixth consecutive weekly climb and the 30-year reached a post-2004 peak on 24 September. WTI is 92.91, down about 1.80%, and Brent 105.14, down about 1.39%, after reports that US and Iranian negotiators are discussing a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Falling oil removes rather than adds an amplifier, though intercepted Houthi missiles over Saudi Arabia and the East-West pipeline shut since 10 September keep the energy track two-sided. European cash is firm, with STOXX 600 +0.7% at 640.66 and DAX +0.6%.

Shared Finviz context collected at 08:12 UTC is partial: the futures and calendar sections were unavailable, so all cross-asset price evidence here comes from independent primary sources. The available sections are latest-session and explicitly not real-time, and are used only as tone confirmation: semiconductors were 7 of 7 positive with a mean of +1.59%, technology +0.55%, and megacaps split 4 to 4 with a mean of +0.235%. Semiconductor leadership without megacap participation is consistent with rotation rather than index-level one-way structure.

Stress rises to 56%. The Nasdaq-100 advance is occurring against a long end that has not backed off, with roughly 77% odds now attached to an October increase after New York Fed President Williams described a further 2026 hike as reasonable, and with the final September Michigan inflation expectations reading due at 14:00 UTC. That is a genuinely difficult environment in which high Stress can coexist with Tail below the blocking threshold. Confidence is 86%: the NQ level and session extremes come from a live primary quote, yields, VIX and oil from primary sources, and the calendar is verified across two independent feeds, with the unavailable Finviz futures section and a stale secondary futures quote the only material gaps.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 published Claude assessments held Tail between 17% and 25%, touching the block threshold once at 09:00 UTC on 24 September during a trend-down European morning before decaying through the US session. Stress stayed elevated in a 54-59% band throughout, reflecting the long-end repricing, and Confidence held between 85% and 88%. From 17:00 UTC the sequence settled into the low Tail band with a normal mode overnight, lifted to the WATCH floor at 06:00 and 07:00 UTC on a trend-up mode as NQ cleared its earlier overnight high, then eased back to 19% at 08:00 UTC when that high stopped extending. This hour the high has advanced again.
outlookSummary: The base case is a continued but orderly grind inside and slightly above a 0.92%-wide overnight band through the European morning, with Tail in the WATCH band on the observed extension and easing where no catalyst sits. Risk concentrates between 12:15 and 15:15 UTC, where August durable goods orders, the US cash open and the final Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations reading fall in sequence into a market pricing roughly 77% odds of an October rate increase. The mode is expected to turn event/whipsaw there, with Tail peaking at 26% and crossing into the block band for two hours around the release and its potential delayed second leg. That peak reflects a credible yields-led mechanism rather than observed structure, and Tail decays quickly if retracements occur and the 10-year holds its range. The afternoon carries a checkpoint at 18:00 UTC with Fed Hammack's remarks and a power hour into the 20:00 UTC cash close on the final session of the week. CME equity index futures then close for the week at 21:00 UTC, so the final twelve forecast hours fall inside a halt: Tail drops to the low band because a halted market cannot produce a pathological path, Stress decays more slowly against carried weekend gap exposure, and Confidence steps down into the medium-low band because no live NQ price path exists to observe.
